subtitle: How a Small Silver Square Spoke Two Worlds at Once

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a Indo-Greek silver coin half-lit, one side with Greek letters, the other hinting Kharosthi, with Apollodotus I's face faintly reflected in the metal
panels.action: Apollodotus I’s calm, thoughtful face hovers in shadow behind a magnified bilingual silver coin, its Greek and Kharosthi legends caught in a shaft of light over a map-like blur of Punjab and the Indus.

dialogue.text: In a land of many tongues, Apollodotus I forged a quiet marvel: a coin that spoke Greek and Kharosthi, one small square binding distant worlds in a shared promise.

i18n.hi: कई ज़बानों की धरती में, अपोलोडोटस प्रथम ने चुपचाप कमाल गढ़ा: सिक्का जो यूनानी और खरोष्ठी बोले, एक छोटा चौकोर जिसने दूर दुनिया को एक वादे में बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot over a map-like panorama from Bactria across the Hindu Kush into the Indus plains, dissolving into busy caravan routes
panels.action: From high above, dusty caravans snake over passes and down into green river plains, while a translucent profile of Apollodotus I looks eastward, superimposed over the routes.

dialogue.text: After the conquests of Demetrios and his kin, the sons of Bactria looked east. Apollodotus I inherited not just spears and horses, but a web of roads stretching from Bactria to the Indus.

i18n.hi: देमेत्रियस और उसके वंश की फतहों के बाद, बाख्त्रिया के बेटे पूरब की तरफ़ देख रहे थे। अपोलोडोटस प्रथम ने सिर्फ़ भाले और घोड़े नहीं, बाख्त्रिया से सिंधु तक फैली राहों का जाल भी पाया।

panels.shot: medium shot in a palace hall at Taxila-like city, mix of Hellenistic and Indian pillars, Apollodotus I in council with Greek and local Indian advisors
panels.action: Apollodotus I sits on a modest throne beneath painted rafters, listening as a Greek official with a scroll and an Indian merchant in a cotton robe gesture in different directions over a clay map.

dialogue.text: In cities like Taxila and the Indus towns, Greek veterans and local guilds shared streets. The king’s orders traveled with translators, carried by men who counted in drachmas and in local weights.

i18n.hi: तक्षशिला और सिंधु काठी के शहरों में, यूनानी सिपाही और स्थानीय संघ एक ही गलियों में थे। राजा के हुक्म दुभाषियों के साथ चलते, ऐसे लोगों के हाथ जो द्राख्मा भी गिनते और देसी बाट भी।

panels.shot: close-up on Apollodotus I leaning over a low table scattered with coins of different shapes and sizes, some round Greek, some square Indian
panels.action: Apollodotus I bends forward, brows furrowed, as his fingers separate round Hellenistic coins from thicker square Indian pieces engraved with elephants and symbols, a lamp casting sharp shadows.

dialogue.text: On his table lay evidence of a problem. Greek round coins of Bactria, Indian square pieces of the Indus—each trusted by some, doubted by others.

i18n.hi: उसकी मेज़ पर एक उलझन पड़ी थी। बाख्त्रिया के गोल यूनानी सिक्के, सिंधु के चौकोर देसी टुकड़े—किसी को अपने, किसी को पराये।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Apollodotus I as he looks at a Greek coin with BASILEOS legend and an Indian coin with no Greek letters
panels.action: Seen from behind his shoulder, Apollodotus I holds up a round coin marked with Greek letters, then sets it beside a locally struck square coin as he glances between them and the horizon beyond the balcony.

dialogue.speaker: apollodotus_i
dialogue.text: One king, two weights, two tongues. Who will trust the same hand?

i18n.hi: एक राजा, दो बाट, दो ज़बानें। एक ही हाथ पर कौन भरोसा करे?

panels.shot: medium shot of a busy market in an Indo-Greek river town, with Greek soldier, Indian craftsman, and caravan trader bargaining
panels.action: In a crowded bazaar, a Greek soldier offers a round drachma, while an Indian artisan weighs a square coin on a small scale, their faces wary as a caravan trader watches, amused and cautious.

dialogue.text: In the markets of Punjab and Sindh, price and trust were argued as fiercely as borders. A Greek coin meant little if a Sindhi potter feared its weight, or could not read its king.

i18n.hi: पंजाब और सिंध की मंडियों में दाम और भरोसा सरहदों जितना सख़्त झगड़ते। अगर सिंधी कुंभार को उसके वजन पर शक हो, या राजा का नाम न पढ़ सके, तो यूनानी सिक्का क्या काम का?

panels.shot: intimate medium shot indoors, Apollodotus I with a local scribe showing palm-leaf with Kharosthi, and a Greek scribe holding wax tablet with Greek
panels.action: Apollodotus I stands between a Kharosthi-writing scribe tracing letters on a palm leaf and a Greek clerk scratching Greek script on a wax tablet, his gaze shifting from one script to the other.

dialogue.text: The scripts themselves told the story. Greek letters for the men from Bactria, Kharosthi for the Gandharan scribes and merchants along the great roads.

i18n.hi: लिपियाँ खुद कहानी कहती थीं। बाख्त्रिया वालों के लिए यूनानी अक्षर, और महान राहों पर चलते गांधारी लिपिकों व व्यापारियों के लिए खरोष्ठी।

panels.shot: close-up on Apollodotus I’s hand sketching a coin design on a wax tablet: Greek legend on one side, Kharosthi on the other
panels.action: His hand presses a stylus into wax, outlining a square coin with a Greek legend on one face and marking the opposite side with flowing strokes to stand for Kharosthi.

dialogue.text: Here the record shows a quiet decision. Apollodotus ordered coins that would carry his title in both tongues: Greek and Kharosthi, silver squares on Indian standards.

i18n.hi: इतिहास यहाँ एक चुप फैसला दिखाता है। अपोलोडोटस ने ऐसे सिक्के गढ़वाए जिन पर उसका खिताब दोनों ज़बानों में हो: यूनानी और खरोष्ठी, देसी मान के चाँदी के चौकोर।

panels.shot: dramatic close-up of an actual bilingual coin being held between thumb and forefinger, Greek side visible with BASILEOS APOLLODOTOU SOTEROS around a symbol
panels.action: Between his fingers gleams a fresh silver coin; the Greek side shows a royal symbol framed by the legend BASILEOS APOLLODOTOU SOTEROS, tiny yet crisp under the workshop light.

dialogue.text: On one face the coin declared, in Greek letters, BASILEOS APOLLODOTOU SOTEROS—‘of King Apollodotus the Saviour’, in the language of his Hellenic soldiers and officials.

i18n.hi: एक रुख़ पर सिक्का यूनानी में ऐलान करता था: बासिलेओस अपोलोडोटोउ सोतेरोस—‘राजा अपोलोडोटस उद्धारक का’, उसके यूनानी सिपाहियों और अफ़सरों की ज़बान में।

panels.shot: rotate to show the reverse side of the same coin, now with Kharosthi script and an elephant or bull design
panels.action: The coin flips in mid-air; the reverse shows an elephant striding, or a bull standing firm, with Kharosthi letters curving around the image.

dialogue.text: On the other face, in Kharosthi script, it answered: Maharajasa Apaladatasa Tratarasa—‘of Great King Apaladata the Protector’, the title translated into the speech of the Indus roads.

i18n.hi: दूसरे रुख़ पर खरोष्ठी में जवाब: महाराजस अपलदतस त्रातरस्—‘महान राजा अपलदत रक्षक का’, वही खिताब सिंधु की राहों की बोली में।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a mint: local artisans striking square coins with elephant and bull imagery under Apollodotus I’s oversight
panels.action: In a mint yard, Indian artisans lift hammers over square flans as Apollodotus I watches from a shaded doorway, dies engraved with elephants, bulls and nandipada symbols lined up on a bench.

dialogue.text: The shapes and signs also shifted. Many pieces were square, not round, matching Indian standards, their elephants, bulls and nandipadas speaking to eyes raised in local shrines as much as in Greek temples.

i18n.hi: आकृतियाँ और निशान भी बदले। कई टुकड़े गोल नहीं, चौकोर बने, देसी मान पर, जिनके हाथी, बैल और नंदिपद स्थानीय मंदिरों और यूनानी देवालयों—दोनों की आँखों से बात करते।

panels.shot: montage wide shot of different hands exchanging the new coin: a Greek officer, a Buddhist monk, a local trader, a caravan leader
panels.action: In three linked vignettes, a Greek officer pays wages, a robed monk accepts alms, and a caravan leader seals a deal, each moment marked by the small glint of an Apollodotus bilingual coin changing hands.

dialogue.text: The coins traveled farther than any herald. Their bilingual promise could be read in garrison courtyards, monastery courtyards and caravanserais from Taxila to the Indus delta.

i18n.hi: ये सिक्के हर एलान से दूर तक गए। उनकी दो-ज़बानी ज़मानत तक्षशिला की छावनियों, विहारों और कारवाँसरायों से लेकर सिंधु डेल्टा तक हर आँगन में पढ़ी गई।

panels.shot: scholarly bird’s-eye view centuries later: a dusty hoard of Indo-Greek coins spread on a modern excavation table, with a faint overlay of the Periplus route map
panels.action: On a modern excavation table, gloved hands arrange Indo-Greek drachmas, while faint lines of an ancient sea route map, echoing the Periplus, hover ghost-like above the hoard.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea would mention old drachmas still known around Barygaza. Its author wrote of memory, not of Apollodotus himself, yet his coins had lingered in trade.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद ‘एरिथ्राई सागर का पेरीप्लस’ बरुगज़ा के पास पुरानी द्राख्माओं का ज़िक्र करेगा। लेखक के पास बस यादें थीं, अपोलोडोटस नहीं, पर उसके सिक्के कारोबार में टिके रहे।

panels.shot: close-up on a numismatist’s tray labeled with Apollodotus I’s issues, emphasising bilingual legends and square shapes
panels.action: A researcher’s tray holds neat rows of Apollodotus’ coins, some round, some square, each labeled, their Greek and Kharosthi legends clearly visible under a magnifying lens.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars, weighing and comparing these pieces, see in Apollodotus’ bilingual issues one of the earliest systematic attempts to bind a mixed realm through shared currency and dual-script titulature.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान, इन्हें तौलते और मिलाते हुए, अपोलोडोटस के दो-ज़बानी सिक्कों को मिली-जुली रियासत को एकजुट करने की सबसे शुरुआती सोच-समझ कर की गई कोशिशों में गिनते हैं—एक ही करंसी, दो लिपियों में खिताब।

panels.shot: abstract split-screen shot: on one side a faint Hellenistic temple front; on the other, an Indian shrine, with a bilingual coin bridging the gap
panels.action: An ethereal image sets a Greek-style portico opposite an Indian shrine niche, the space between them crossed by the silhouette of a single bilingual coin, suspended like a small, solid bridge.

dialogue.text: The elephants and bulls upon them may have signaled many things—regional pride, religious echoes, royal imagery. The record does not fix one meaning, but the bridge of language upon them is clear.

i18n.hi: इन पर बने हाथी और बैल कई इशारे कर सकते थे—इलाके का गर्व, धर्म की गूँज, राजसत्ता की छवि। मतलब तय नहीं, पर जो ज़बानों का पुल इन पर है, वो साफ़ दिखाई देता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Apollodotus I at a balcony at dusk, looking over a river port where ships and caravans meet
panels.action: At dusk, Apollodotus I stands at a balcony rail above a river port where masts and camel caravans crowd together, his hand resting lightly on a small pouch of coins tied at his belt.

dialogue.speaker: apollodotus_i
dialogue.text: Steel conquers a day. Silver and words must hold the years.

i18n.hi: फ़ौलाद दिन जीतता है। सालों को थामना चाँदी और लफ़्ज़ों का काम है।

panels.shot: final contemplative close-up on a single Apollodotus bilingual coin resting on an open palm, with faint reflections of scripts around it
panels.action: A weathered open palm holds a single Apollodotus bilingual coin against a soft, unfocused background; faint ghostly lines of Greek and Kharosthi script shimmer around it like whispers.

dialogue.text: Apollodotus I’s bilingual coin shows how power can travel not only by sword, but by weight, script and symbol—and how good rule, in any age, must learn to speak in the languages people use.

i18n.hi: अपोलोडोटस प्रथम का दो-ज़बानी सिक्का दिखाता है कि ताकत सिर्फ़ तलवार से नहीं, वजन, लिपि और निशान से भी चलती है—और अच्छा राज, हर ज़माने में, लोगों की बोली सीखकर ही ज़िंदा रहता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Small Silver Square Spoke Two Worlds at Once
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक छोटा चाँदी का चौकोर दो दुनिया से एक साथ बोला
